Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the CAIQ draft you shared earlier. We're working through the Brightpath security review and have a couple of control-specific asks before we lock the assessment:

1) Tenant isolation: we need a control-level mapping and evidence that shows network/compute isolation between tenants, including any ephemeral KV caches and whether those caches are ever written to durable storage. A network diagram +ACL export would be ideal.

Alex — thanks for the questions. Quick clarifications below and next steps:

- Automatic snapshots: Redwood does NOT perform automatic continuous backups of ephemeral KV caches as part of normal processing. Cache contents are TTL-purged; occasional diagnostic snapshots are performed only when explicitly triggered by engineering for root-cause analysis or when a customer-authorized support session requests it. Those snapshots are tagged, access-controlled, and scheduled for deletion; retention for those artifacts is 30 days by default unless a customer signs an exception.

- Contract / warranty language: We can provide a short attestatory statement confirming the default non-persistence behavior and the operational retention windows (TTL purge + diagnostic snapshot retention). We cannot offer an absolute warranty that supersedes our SLA terms, but Legal can sign a supplementary attestation letter. If Brightpath needs a DocuSign attestation, please confirm the exact language and we'll route to Legal.

- Audit sample: Marissa has uploaded an additional sample line showing the tenant-id redaction pattern; see runtime_audit_sample.log in the bundle.

Next step: I propose a 20-minute call tomorrow 08:30 PT to walk through the mapping and the attestation wording. Rishi will coordinate scheduling — copying him here.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Head of Compliance Operations — Redwood Inference
